questions.q: How does an accounting attribute differ from a source, as described in this lesson?
options: They are the exact same concept with two names
A source is data available from the transaction; an accounting attribute is a specific value SLA itself requires by name (like Accounting Date) to build a journal entry
Accounting attributes only exist in Receivables, never in Payables
Sources are required, while accounting attributes are always optional
questions.explain: Sources are available transaction data; accounting attributes are specific, named values SLA needs, with an assignment wiring a source to each required attribute.

questions.q: What is the difference between a header-level and a line-level accounting attribute?
options: There is no real difference; all attributes behave identically
Header-level attributes only exist for Fixed Assets
Line-level attributes can never vary between lines on the same entry
A header-level attribute (like Accounting Date) applies once per journal entry, while a line-level attribute (like Entered Amount) applies individually to each line
questions.explain: Header-level attributes apply once to the whole entry; line-level attributes can differ from line to line, since lines can have different amounts or types.

questions.q: What happens if a required accounting attribute, like Entered Amount, has no valid assignment for an event class?
options: Nothing; required attributes are purely cosmetic
The transaction is automatically deleted
The General Ledger ignores the missing attribute and posts anyway
SLA cannot build a complete journal entry for that event class without a valid assignment
questions.explain: Required accounting attributes must have a valid source assignment, or SLA cannot construct a complete journal entry for events of that class.

questions.q: At what level are most accounting attribute assignments defaulted, according to this lesson?
options: At the individual journal line rule level only
At the event class level, through Oracle's seeded configuration
At the ledger's calendar setup
Accounting attributes have no default and must always be manually assigned from scratch
questions.explain: Most accounting attribute assignments default at the event class level, often already sensibly configured by Oracle.

questions.q: Where can an accounting attribute's default assignment be overridden, if needed?
options: It can never be overridden under any circumstances
Only by contacting Oracle Support to change the Fusion codebase
Only by changing the ledger's currency
On a journal line type, or within a specific Application Accounting Definition
questions.explain: Depending on the attribute, the event-class default can be overridden at a more specific level, such as a journal line type or a particular AAD.
